course_name_original: FOUNDATION OF MATHEMATICAL ANALYSIS AND PROBABILITY (INL1001825)
course_name_en: Foundation of Mathematical Analysis and Probability
prerequisites: Differential and integral calculus in one variable

learning_outcomes.text: Recall, recognize, and contextualize the mathematical tools developed during the course
Present definitions and statements, using mathematical language consciously and correctly
Argue the proofs indicated in the detailed course syllabus
Solve problems of similar type and difficulty to those covered in class and proposed for practice during the course, possibly with some new elements for higher grades

Explain the solution of problems of similar type and difficulty to those covered in class and proposed for practice during the course, using appropriate terminology and making precise reference to theorems from the course
Recognize the usefulness of applying some of the course tools in other disciplines, such as physics
Critical and analytical thinking, including the ability to engage with artificial intelligence
Problem-solving skills, or the ability to explore and present possible strategies
The ability to compute relevant quantities of the mathematical objects introduced
Optionally, evaluation skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in a team

syllabus_topics: Graphs of functions of several variables, level curves
Limits of functions of several variables
Differential calculus for functions of several variables
Curves and their length, line integrals
Vector fields, conservative fields, Green’s theorem, divergence theorem
Probability: definition and basic properties, probability on finite sets and combinatorial calculus
Discrete random variables. Binomial, geometrical and Poisson random variables, Poisson approximation
Continuous random variables. Exponential and uniform variables. Normal random variables
Markov and Chebyshev inequalities, law of large numbers
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)
Peer assessment (solving exercises and reviewing work of other students)

assessment_methods.method: Written examination (quizzes on Moodle Esami with justifications)
Formative assessment (online and in-class activities for "Follower" mode)
Peer review on first integrals (for "Traditional" mode)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the average of the skills test (solving exercises) and the knowledge test (theorems and definitions). The oral examination requires correctly answering at least one of two theoretical questions and is a prerequisite for the written examination. The written examination consists of quizzes with written justifications; incorrect or incomplete reasoning results in no credit. "Follower" mode includes continuous engagement and online activities, potentially offering a bonus to increase the final grade or reduce the scope of the final test, valid only for the winter exam session. "Traditional" mode involves only the final in-class test and a peer review on first integrals. An additional oral examination may be required at the discretion of the examination board. For honors, an oral validation and achieving the maximum score in the written examination are required.
